A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MapEval, with matching core datasets, experiments, and extensive appendices. Text, tables, figures, and qualitative examples are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model and human evaluations, error analyses, and calculator and Chameleon experiments, including Tables 3–7 and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds visual-model evaluations, open-ended evaluation, and fine-tuning experiments in Tables 5, 13, and 14.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, cached-map environment, ReAct evaluation, calculator augmentation, and Chameleon approach are retained. Calculator and Chameleon experiments already appear in v1. The added standard instruction-tuning study evaluates adaptation of existing models rather than introducing a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The underlying 700 questions, geographical coverage, modalities, and geospatial categories remain unchanged. Appendix G.2 adds an open-ended scenario for textual and visual questions by removing answer choices, requiring answer generation instead of option selection. The fine-tuning split does not introduce new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds Qwen2.5-VL-72B and Llama3.2-90B-Vision to the visual comparison. Appendix G.3 also compares five existing textual models with their instruction-tuned counterparts. The established textual, API, calculator, and Chameleon comparison sets are otherwise retained; o3-mini serves as a grader, not a competing system.

E3.justification: Two substantive evaluation designs are added. Appendix G.2 evaluates Claude-3.5-Sonnet without answer options, grades responses using o3-mini, and describes manual checking. Appendix G.3 randomly divides the 300 textual questions into 97 training and 203 test questions for before-and-after instruction-tuning comparisons. These supplement the retained main MCQ protocols.

E4.justification: New analyses test dependence on answer choices and whether limited task-specific training alleviates benchmark difficulty, including an examination of automatic-grader errors. Visual category and zoom analyses gain two models. The qualitative appendix also revises Listing 12 and replaces v1's travel-time example with hospital-selection and nearest-museum examples; earlier calculator and error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed values, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added random train/test split and manual grading inspection do not introduce uncertainty estimation. The existing annotation-agreement and human-scoring descriptions remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing main-table model scores are retained, but substantial results are added. Table 5 reports Qwen2.5-VL-72B at 60.35%, replacing Qwen2-VL-7B at 51.63% as the best evaluated open-source visual model. Table 13 adds open-ended textual/visual accuracies of 55.33%/51.88%. Table 14 reports mixed fine-tuning effects, including Gemma-2.0-9B rising from 46.80% to 51.23% on the new 203-question test split. These are new comparisons, not improvements to v1's unchanged full-benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal propositions, proofs, or a theoretical analysis. The Haversine-distance and bearing computations described in v1 Appendix I remain in v2 Appendix G.1 without substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains the same three-mode MapEval benchmark and the finding that foundation models struggle with geospatial reasoning and substantially trail humans. The rewritten abstract updates the evaluated-model count and foregrounds the 67% accuracy ceiling, but does not redefine the core scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix G.2 adds discussion of open-ended applicability, grading unreliability, and evaluation cost, including 55% automatic versus approximately 80% manually assessed accuracy for textual unanswerable responses. G.3 interprets small fine-tuning gains as evidence of difficulties beyond training exposure. Existing API-coverage, generalization, and prompt limitations are retained under the Impact Statement.

D1.justification: v2 provides a project-website reference and direct repositories for the three tasks, and Table 11 documents parameter counts and context windows for the added visual models. Existing tool descriptions, cache details, and example prompts are retained. The new fine-tuning study identifies standard instruction tuning but supplies no detailed training hyperparameters.

R1.justification: v2 adds model references such as the Qwen2.5-VL technical report, Phi-3 report, and Claude-3.5 announcement, and replaces the earlier Llama analysis citation with a Meta model-card citation. The substantive related-work discussion in Section 2 and Appendix A remains largely unchanged; publication and author-metadata updates do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and results discussion are extensively rewritten and condensed, while Section 5 separates failure descriptions from enhancement approaches. Reproducibility and limitations sections are consolidated into an Impact Statement. Appendices are substantially reordered, moving qualitative examples after dataset statistics, supplementary experiments, and result visualizations.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column conference formatting, with widespread table and figure resizing and relocation. Figure 1 is redrawn, geographical and zoom-performance figures move to the appendix, and result tables gain sample-count headers. New Tables 13–14, expanded visual-model charts, and changed illustrated examples substantially revise the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the benchmark with more competitive visual baselines and useful tests of answer-format dependence and training exposure that v1 lacked. It also explicitly exposes automatic-grading limitations. These gains are limited by sparse fine-tuning details and incomplete integration of new findings: Section 4.2.3 still describes 47.73% as the best counting accuracy despite Table 5 reporting 52.33% for Qwen2.5-VL-72B. The added evidence improves the paper overall, but does not resolve its main validation and reproducibility limitations.
